title: Multisensory Perception Of Architectural Design
review_question: To understand the human senses and how architectural design impacts their perception of space, and to comprehend how people's senses respond to built environments.
inclusion_exclusion_criteria: Recent research papers and review articles published in journals between 2017 and 2021 were considered, focusing on four human senses and their relation to perception theory.

synthesis_conclusions: Including multimodal perception in architectural design creates comprehensive and fulfilling experiences by purposefully appealing to sight, sound, touch, smell, and even taste.
Architects can elicit emotional reactions, direct movement, and develop a sense of connection by carefully balancing materials, textures, lighting, acoustics, and spatial arrangements.
User-centered design, which recognizes and accounts for people's preferences and requirements, is crucial for providing inclusion and accessibility.
Multisensory design improves not only the aesthetic and practical features of architecture but also the well-being and quality of life of individuals who use these places.

Architecture's pursuit of multimodal perception can inspire, engage, and resonate on a profoundly human level, fostering a peaceful and meaningful cohabitation between people and the built environment.
